author: Lal Chand Singh, Patna Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Kolhua (Muzaffarpur), the Asoka pillar site N of Vaisali
evidence: 1996-97 season N and W of the Markat Hrid tank: over eighty votive stupas (circular, square, composite), small square shrine, common rammed brick-jelly floor sloping to the tank; standing sandstone Buddha c. 60 cm
quote: carried out excavation at the site towards north and west of the Markat Hrid tank … one partly damaged sandstone image of Buddha in the standing posture
note: No Xuanzang reference and no inscription. The site of Mizutani's 07.03.04 (Asoka stupa and pillar at Kolhua); the tank is the one the ASR (Cunningham) and the AR (Bloch, Ram-kund) take for the monkey tank. Continued in 575, 590.
Bhita excavation and a Mughal pool; Ahichchhatra only as a pottery type; no Xiyu ji place located.
Exploration list for Basti/Siddharthnagar (Birdpur, 9 km S of Piprahwa: brick stupa); no identification argued.

author: B. R. Mani, Excavation Branch II, ASI
asr_identification: Nautanwa (Maharajganj, then Gorakhpur area, NE of Siddharthnagar) = Nivartana chaitya where Siddhartha sent Chandaka and Kanthaka back; Sankisa excavation begins
evidence: two seasons' exploration in Basti and Siddharthnagar: sites matched with Pali-text places by size, antiquity, name similarity and geography (Behil = Vehalinga, Siswania = Simsapavana of Setavya, Mehdawal = Medalumpa, Saltauwa = Salavatika, Kaudiram = Koliyagrama, Nautanwa = Nivartana chaitya); no excavation at Nautanwa
quote: These identifications have been based on the size and antiquity of sites, similarities in the ancient and present names and their geographical locations … towards further north-east the township of Nautanwa with ancient Nivartana chaitya from where Siddhartha returned Chhandaka and Kanthaka back to Kapilavastu
note: Nautanwa for the place where the prince sent back Chandaka (Xuanzang's stupa, 06.03.03) is new: Mizutani (uncertain) puts it on the Anoma bank in the Moriya territory, Cunningham (asr) at mounds by the Kudawa Nala. The basis is name and geography only. Kaudiram = Koliyagrama is not Xuanzang's Ramagrama (06.03). The Sankisa report starts here; detail in 563.; 04.15 removed (the identification is the Nautanwa = Nivartana proposal, 06.03.03)

author: B. R. Mani, Excavation Branch II, ASI
asr_identification: Sankisa (Farrukhabad): sacred Buddhist area with the Asokan elephant capital and the so-called stupa mound
evidence: second season: NBPW to Gupta occupation; room W of the elephant-capital site in three phases (pre-Kushan bricks 53-54 cm reused), probably part of a monastery of Maurya-Gupta date; trenches NE of the 'so-called Stupa mound' disturbed by Cunningham's digging (1853 coin), pre-Kushan brick structure, thick brick debris = important building nearby
quote: This room may be a part of a monastery which seems to have existed from Maurya to Gupta period … It is quite evident that these trenches abutting the brick mound, supposed to be the main stupa, containing thick deposit of brick debris in the topmost layer, point to some important construction in the close vicinity
note: Supports Sankisa as a Buddhist site from Maurya to Gupta, as Mizutani (04.15, disputed) and Cunningham (asr, Sankisa; elephant capital possibly Xuanzang's pillar). No inscription naming Kapitha/Samkasya and no statement on Xuanzang's descent stairs (04.15.02).

author: L. C. Singh, Excavation Branch III Patna, ASI, with Kansai University (Y. Abosi)
asr_identification: Maheth = the city of Sravasti (Sravasti district)
evidence: Area E of Maheth: two house-complexes either side of a 2-2.5 m N-S street, Period III (early CE to 4th c. AD); 664 antiquities, local Ayodhya coins, seals and sealings in Kushan Brahmi (not read in the report)
quote: resumed excavation at Maheth (Area E) in eight quadrants upto a depth of Period III … An evidence of massive building-complex belonging to Period III, i.e., from early Christian era to the fourth century AD, was exposed
note: Maheth = Sravasti as Mizutani (06.01), asr and ar; secular city remains, no inscription naming the city. Continued in 565.
Continuation of 564 (Sravasti Maheth Area E): pottery, figures and plates; the Kushan Brahmi seals are not read. Then Pakhanna = Pushkarana (not a Xiyu ji place).
Museums (Kausambi arrow-heads at Allahabad; Bodhgaya Museum).
Museums (Mathura, Sarnath).
Conservation (Murshidabad, Thanesar Pather Masjid and Sheikh Chilli's tomb).
Conservation; 'Rangamati' here is Rangamati in Dhubri, Assam, not Karnasuvarna's Rangamati.
Conservation (Amaravati Mahastupa fencing).
Conservation (Piprahwa monastery, Sahet tank, Kolhua main stupa).
Archaeological chemistry (Kushinagar monasteries, Sarnath, Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda sculptures).
Gardens and publications (Srivastava's Piprahwa and Ganwaria memoir listed, no content).

author: Muhammed K. K., Patna Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Kesariya stupa mound (East Champaran)
evidence: first season on the NE slope (16 trenches): terraced circular brick stupa, three terraces with rows of cells holding stucco Buddhas (dhyana and bhumisparsa), decorative fills; three phases (earth-filled terraces; added cells and polygonal patterns; British repairs); dated to the 7th c. on pottery, images and architecture
quote: took up excavation work at the lofty mound of Kesariya with a view to understand the nature of mound and to expose the expected structure of stupa as reported in the earlier reports of Cunningham … On the basis of pottery, images and the architectural pattern, the present stupa could be assigned to the seventh century
note: Mizutani 07.03.13 (Kesariya, agreed; asr Cunningham, ar Page). A 7th-c. date would make the terraced stupa about Xuanzang's time; later seasons (589, 620) give a Sunga-Kushan core with late-Gupta cells. No inscription. The passage also starts the Taradih (Bodh Gaya) report, which is not linked to a Xuanzang site.

author: Muhammed K. K., Patna Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Kolhua (Muzaffarpur), Asoka pillar site
evidence: W and N of the tank: three more votive stupas and rammed floor; 10 x 40 m area NE of the Asokan pillar: 1.40 m walls and cells with entrance, i.e. another monastery
quote: A small area of 10 x 40 m has also been taken up towards north-east of the Asokan pillar which has revealed 1.40 m thick walls, cells with entrance, some red ware potsherds, terracotta balls and two nut-shaped beads, indicating the existence of another monastery
note: Agrees with Mizutani 07.03.04; monastic buildings round the pillar fit the monastery remains Xuanzang reports near the Asoka stupa and pillar, but the report does not say so. Continues 559.
Kanaganahalli stupa panels and Bekal Fort; 'hadda' an OCR or string match; no Xiyu ji place.
Jhusi and exploration list for Allahabad/Kausambi districts; no location argued.

author: G. T. Shendey, Excavation Branch III Patna, ASI, and A. Abosi, Kansai University
asr_identification: Mahet = fortified city of Sravasti
evidence: Kandbhari Gate (SE of the Mahet fortification): brick walls of the entrance (87 m), three building phases, brickbat pathway; Chirenath temple mound outside the walls
quote: Kandbhari Gate is located in the south-east of the fortified area of Mahet. The aim of excavation was to expose the entrance of fortification
note: Agrees with Mizutani 06.01 (Sahet-Mahet). City defences only; no inscription. Continued in 579-580.
Continuation of 578 (Sravasti, Kandbhari Gate): pottery Periods I-III, plans and plates.
Continuation of 578: Chirenath (Siva) temple outside Mahet; Period II cells 'might be a part of some monastery', Kanishka coin; no identification.

author: Muhammed K. K., Patna Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Chaukhandi stupa mound, Sarnath (Varanasi)
evidence: five trenches at the SE corner: 1.30 m outer walls of the terraces and 1.10 m cross walls forming earth-filled boxes; Gupta-period terraced brick structure (after Cunningham and Oertel)
quote: carried out excavation work at Chaukhandi stupa mound in Sarnath. As per the excavations by Cunningham and Oertel, this lofty brick structure of Gupta period consists of three square terraces raised one above the other
note: Agrees with Mizutani 07.01.10 and with Cunningham (asr) and the AR (Chaukhandi = the stupa SW of the Deer Park monastery); dig for restoration, no identification argued. Continued in 597.
Other discoveries: votive stupa found NW of the Amaravati Mahastupa while fencing; Kotturu relic casket. No location argued (Amaravati = Mizutani 10.14.02a).
Museums: Mathura Museum acquires a pillar base of Huvishka's year 33 recording a gift to the Sarvastivadins' vihara by brahmans of Takshasila; no location of a Xiyu ji place argued.
Conservation (Katra mosque, Murshidabad; Agroha).
Conservation (Sahet tank, Kausambi structures near the Asokan pillar).
Conservation (Kolhua stupas, Nalanda, Kumrahar, Kushinagar, Chaukhandi).
Archaeological chemistry (votive stupas NE of the Dhamekh stupa, Sarnath).
Publications and index to Ancient India (Ahichchhatra, Taxila, Rajgir articles listed).

author: Muhammed K. K., Patna Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Kesariya stupa (East Champaran)
evidence: second season (18 new trenches): five brick-veneered terraces; two brick sizes = Sunga-Kushan and late-Gupta phases plus British repairs; base circle over 100 m across; nine cells to the third terrace, each with a large seated Buddha on a platform, Gupta/late-Gupta mouldings
quote: it is clear that the stupa was constructed in five terraces veneered with bricks laid in mud-mortar … representing two phases, Sunga-Kushan and late Gupta period respectively … The base circle measures over 100 m in diameter
note: Agrees with Mizutani 07.03.13. The Sunga-Kushan core with late-Gupta cells revises the 7th-c. date of 574; either way the stupa stood in Xuanzang's day. No inscription.

author: Muhammed K. K., Patna Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Kolhua (Muzaffarpur): svastika-shaped monastery, tank, votive stupas
evidence: pathway (brick-jelly in lime-surkhi) between the svastika-shaped monastery and the tank; brick steps of the monastery gate; strip N of the remains with votive stupas and plastered floor; finds Gupta and late Gupta
quote: Area in-between the svastika- shaped monastery and the tank was taken up this year which revealed a connecting pathway between the two
note: Agrees with Mizutani 07.03.04 (Kolhua pillar site; tank = the monkey tank in asr/ar). The Gupta-late Gupta monastery fits Xuanzang's date; not linked to him in the report. The passage opens with the end of the Kesariya report (589).

author: D. S. Malik and M. Acharya, Department of Archaeology and Museums, Haryana
asr_identification: Sugh (Amadalpur), c. 5 km E of Jagadhri (Yamuna Nagar)
evidence: first regular excavation (nine trenches, 1-4 m): four periods from PGW (800-500 BC) on; objective to correlate the literary evidence (Taittiriya Aranyaka, Mahabharata, Varahamihira, Divyavadana, Hiuen Tsang's Asokan pillar and monastery) with the finds
quote: enjoyed a considerable importance during the ancient times when it was known as Srughna … Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang found an Asokan pillar and a monastery here in the seventh century AD. Thereafter till about the twelveth century it remained an important place
note: Sugh = Srughna as Mizutani (04.09, agreed) and Cunningham (asr). The excavation takes the identification as settled; no Asokan pillar or monastery found this season.
Kanispur (Kashmir): goblet compared with Sirkap finds at Taxila; plates.
Agiabir excavation and Mirzapur exploration; Ahichchhatra, Bhita, Kausambi as comparanda only.

author: G. T. Shendey, Excavation Branch III Patna, ASI, and Takahiro Takahasi, Kansai University
asr_identification: Maheth = fortified city of Sravasti
evidence: Kandbhari Gate: enclosure wall c. 80 m, small bastion, three security points and the complete entrance complex leading into Maheth; brick-paved footpath
quote: resulting in the discovery of massive enclosure wall (pl.78), three security points and complete entrance-complex leading towards the fortified city of Maheth
note: Agrees with Mizutani 06.01. City gate only; the Kushan sealings (one read 'sivadevasa', plates in 596) do not name the city. Continued in 595-596.
Continuation of 594 (Sravasti gate-complex): phases, finds, plates.
Continuation of 594: periods (1st c. BC-12th c. AD) and plates (Kushan sealing 'sivadevasa'); then Uttarkashi exploration.

author: Muhammed K. K., Patna Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Chaukhandi stupa, Sarnath (Varanasi)
evidence: E side: 2 m wide brick-paved pathway to the centre = at least one E gateway; traces of a pradakshinapatha at the SE corner
quote: carried out excavation on the eastern side of Choukhandi Stupa … indicating that this stupa had atleast one gateway towards east
note: Continues 581; agrees with Mizutani 07.01.10. No identification argued.
Museums (Mathura acquisitions).
Conservation (Lakshmanesvara temple, Sirpur).
Conservation (Nalanda votive stupas, temples, monasteries).
Archaeological chemistry (Kolhua).
Archaeological chemistry (Kushinagara, Sarnath votive stupas near the Dhamekh).
Title page, cover and preface (Sirpur on the back cover).

author: Muhammed K. K., Patna Circle (Kesariya) and Excavation Branch III Patna (Rajgir), ASI
asr_identification: Kesariya stupa (East Champaran); terraced brick stupa in the mound 200 m N of the SW gate of old Rajgir (Nalanda)
evidence: Kesariya: five terraces with cells, drum 9.38 m high and c. 22 m across with ayaka projections, possible lower terrace. Rajgir: mound c. 40 m across inside the SW gate near the chariot-rut marks; red, grey, NBP and Kaolin wares; terraced brick stupa (lower terrace 29 x 25 m with buttresses), brick chambers and an apsidal structure like that at Jivakamravana
quote: Atop the fifth terrace rises the stupa to a height of 9.38 meters having a dia of about 22 meters … The mound is 200 m north from the southwestern gate of the ancient Rajgir and 100 m south of the chariot wheel marks and shell inscriptions … The excavation laid bare the remains of a terraced brick stupa
note: Kesariya as Mizutani 07.03.13. The Vanganga stupa lies inside old Rajagrha (Kusagrapura, Mizutani 09.02.04, agreed); the report does not link it to any of Xuanzang's stupas in the old city. Continued in 621.
Kabra-Kala exploration ('water routes connected with the ancient Pataliputra') and Hella Bazar, Hajipur; no location argued.
Bijamandal temple ('bhita' a moulding name); no Xiyu ji place.

author: Jagat Pati Joshi and A. K. Sharma, Bodhisattva Nagarjuna Smarak Sanstha Va Anusandhan Kendra, Nagpur
asr_identification: Sirpur (Mahasamund): Buddhist temple and vihara (nunnery) inside the fortified area S of the Raikera tank
evidence: W-facing Buddha temple with central shrine (1.45 m granite Buddha, bhumisparsa) and two side shrines, attached vihara of 12+ rooms round a 16-pillared mandapa inside a stone enclosure; glass bangles = nunnery; Brahmi mason's marks of the 5th c. AD; Khalji coins at the top
quote: revealed a west facing Buddha Temple along with vihara upto the plinth level … Mason's marks in the from of alphabets in Brahmi datable to the fifth century AD, were noticed on the top slabs of the plinth
note: Buddhist monastery at Sirpur dated from the 5th c. by mason's marks: supports Mizutani's (disputed) capital of Kosala at Sirpur (10.12) and Xuanzang's monasteries there more directly than the 8th-c. Anandaprabhu vihara of the earlier IAR; asr (Cunningham) only Chhattisgarh. Not linked to Xuanzang in the report.
Continuation of 607 (Sirpur: tilted Buddha, wall orientation, Acheulian tools), then Sanchi.

author: S. V. Venkateshaiah, Aurangabad Circle, ASI
asr_identification: right bank of the Waghora opposite Caves 4 and 17, Ajanta (Aurangabad)
evidence: debris clearance: possible votive stupa on a brick platform; two parallel E-W brick walls (14.72 m) with a row of five cells, central shrine cell with a pedestal enlarged in a second phase; bricks as at Bhokardan (Satavahana-Vakataka)
quote: carried out scientific debris clearance work on the right bank of River Waghora, opposite of Cave 4 … forming a row of five cells
note: Structural monastery facing the Ajanta caves (Mizutani 11.03.03, agreed); not linked to Xuanzang. Continued in 624.
Sikri (Fatehpur Sikri) Jaina temple; Kankali Tila, Mathura only as comparison.

author: R. S. Fonia and Syed Jamal Hasan, Lucknow Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Orajhar mound (Balrampur), Cunningham's Purvarama at Sravasti
evidence: small dig in the centre and S of the mound to recheck Cunningham's sequence and trace the Purvarama: Period I Kushan monastic complex of uniform cells with brick floors, entrances and stairs; Period II Gupta temple plinth (6.20 m) with pilasters like the Sahet temple; Period III later platforms and a star-shaped temple plinth
quote: besides tracing the remains of 'Purvarama' or Eastern monastery' of lady Vishakha, a disciple of Lord Buddha … Period I revealed a monastic-complex in the form of small cells of Kushan period
note: Tests Cunningham's Ora-jhar = Purvarama (asr, 06.01): a Kushan monastery is found, but no inscription and the report does not decide. Purvarama is Faxian's; Xuanzang has only the stupa where the Buddha accepted Visakha's invitation; no separate id in places.tsv.
Excavation in the mid-Ganga (Red Polished ware; Kausambi as comparison); Tokwa.
Jagajjibanpur (Tulabhita) Pala monastery 'Nanda-dirghi'; not a Xiyu ji place.
Numismatics and other discoveries (Barabhita, Assam); 'bhita' a string match.
Conservation (Amaravati, Nagarjunakonda fort).
Conservation (Kolhua, Nalanda, Rajgir newly excavated stupa, Kumrahar).
Gardens and publications (Chaukhandi, Sarnath, Kankali Tila).
Title page and cover (Sravasti and Ajanta plaques).
Director General's preface (Sravasti excavation mentioned; Thanesar museum).

author: Muhammed K. K., Patna Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Kesariya stupa (East Champaran)
evidence: drum and upper two terraces cleared; concealed 80 cm staircase at the SW; more groups of three cells on the lower terraces; head of a stucco Buddha dated to the Gupta period
quote: Noticeable is the head of a stucco image which throws light, for the first time, on the facial features of the image confirming it to be of Gupta period
note: Agrees with Mizutani 07.03.13; a Gupta-period cell image confirms the stupa with its Buddha images stood before Xuanzang. The passage goes on to Chandimao (not a Xiyu ji site).

author: Muhammed K. K., Excavation Branch III Patna, ASI
asr_identification: terraced brick stupa at the southern tip of old Rajgir (Nalanda)
evidence: stupa fully exposed: lower terrace 29 x 25 m with buttresses, robber's trench, upper terrace of brick chambers with an apsidal structure (13.20 x 2.40 m) like the Jivakamravana one; NBP and Kaolin wares, Brahmi fragment with incised bull; dated early Mauryan
quote: the mound near Banganga at the southern tip of Rajgir was taken up for excavation … A terraced-brick stupa was exposed completely … On the basis of the above finds the site may be assigned to the early Mauryan period
note: Continues 604. An early Mauryan stupa inside old Rajagrha (Mizutani 09.02.04, agreed); no identification with a stupa of Xuanzang's account.
Exploration in Junagadh: 'Mathura' is a village in Gujarat.
Ambaran (Jammu) relic stupa compared with Taxila stupas (Dharmarajika, Kalwan, Jandial); no Xiyu ji place located.

author: S. V. Venkateshaiah, Aurangabad Circle, ASI
asr_identification: right bank of the Waghora overlooking Caves 4 and 17, Ajanta (Aurangabad)
evidence: U-shaped brick vihara with cells on three sides opening towards the river; finds incl. a Vakataka-style Mahishasuramardini plaque and a gold coin of Theodosius (AD 402-450) from the disuse phase; dated 4th-5th c. AD
quote: A brick-built monastery (vihara) in 'U' shape (pl. 73) consists of row of cells on three sides … Based on the pottery and the adhishthana mouldings on the brick wall of the monastery, the site can be dated between AD fourth and fifth century
note: Continues 609. A structural monastery of the 4th-5th c. facing the Ajanta caves (Mizutani 11.03.03, agreed); no link to Xuanzang's account in the report. Rest of the report in 625.
Continuation of 624 (Ajanta finds and dating), then exploration of the cave pathways and Ellora.

author: G. C. Chauley, Excavation Branch III Patna, ASI
asr_identification: Maheth = fortified city of Sravasti
evidence: 100 m inside the Kandbhari Gate: residential area with a 9 m wide rammed road (pre-Mauryan/Mauryan) from the Kandbhari to the Naushahara Gate, lime kiln, wells; Kushan and Gupta houses; temple area 200 m NW of the gate with a Gupta panchayatana brick temple
quote: conducted excavation at Maheth mound at Sravasti … Most important discovery of this period is a 9m long, 8.3m wide ancient road … The temple area, about 200m north-west of Kandbhari Gate inside the fortified city of Maheth
note: Agrees with Mizutani 06.01; city remains, no inscription naming Sravasti. Continued in 627-628.
Continuation of 626 (Sravasti houses and wells, plates).
Continuation of 626 (Sravasti: Gupta panchayatana temple inside Maheth, plates).
Epigraphy: 'Mathura-sima' in a Vijayanagara charter (Tamil Nadu).
Numismatics (Khalji coins from Sirpur; Mathura mint).
Museums (Thanesar museum for the Harsha-ka-Tila finds).
Architectural survey (temples at Sirpur; Katra Wazir Khan, Agra).
Conservation; Rangamati mosque, Dhubri (Assam).
Conservation (Kesariya, Kolhua, Nalanda, new Rajgir stupa, Kumrahar).
Science and gardens (Bodh Gaya rock sample, Ajanta plaster).
